books.section: Great Depression and the New Deal (1929–1939)

options.misconception: The repeal of federal regulation illustrates Roosevelt's approach.
options.text: The repeal of all federal regulation of business

options.misconception: A national sales tax illustrates Roosevelt's approach.
options.text: The establishment of a national sales tax on all goods

options.misconception: Abolishing the Federal Reserve illustrates Roosevelt's approach.
options.text: The abolition of the Federal Reserve System
The Civilian Conservation Corps providing jobs and conservation work

rationales.A: Repealing all federal regulation is the opposite of the New Deal.
rationales.B: No national sales tax on all goods was established.
rationales.C: The Federal Reserve was not abolished.
rationales.D: Background: the Civilian Conservation Corps is a textbook New Deal program, federal jobs, conservation work, and direct relief. Young men planted trees, built trails, and sent wages home to their families.
rationales.general:
1. Name the approach. Active federal action providing relief, recovery, and reform.
2. Look for a program that fits. Background: the CCC gave federal jobs and conservation work, direct relief.
3. Test the inventions. No repeal of regulation, no national sales tax, and no abolition of the Federal Reserve occurred.
4. Match the illustration. The CCC is federal action doing relief work.
Remember: an illustration must be a real program that fits the approach.

source: original; stimulus is a verbatim public-domain excerpt from Franklin D. Roosevelt, First Inaugural Address (1933)
stem: Which of the following New Deal developments most directly illustrates the approach Roosevelt described?

stimulus.source_note: Franklin D. Roosevelt, First Inaugural Address, March 4, 1933, public domain.
stimulus.text: I am convinced that the only thing we have to fear is fear itself — nameless, unreasoning, unjustified terror which paralyzes needed efforts to convert retreat into advance.
